task.description: REWORK ITERATION 2. TEST-RUNNER's recheck (step-04-test-run-recheck.json) found a NEW, genuinely-reproduced flake (1-of-4 scripts/test_parallel.sh runs) in test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs's AC-5 test 'the running script is a child of Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor while in flight' (around lines 388-407). It structurally uses a single fixed `Process.sleep(50)` followed by one non-retrying `Task.Supervisor.children/1` check to observe the script mid-flight -- under real host load contention (measured: loadavg near/above core count, DB query queueing 52ms+), a fixed 50ms sleep is not a reliable synchronization primitive; the in-flight window can be missed or the process can already be gone by the time the check runs, or conversely might not yet have started, depending on scheduler timing. Fix: replace the fixed-sleep-then-single-check pattern with a short poll/retry loop (e.g. repeatedly check Task.Supervisor.children/1 with a small sleep between attempts, up to a bounded total wait well under the test's own configured timeout_ms) so the assertion becomes robust to scheduling jitter without weakening what it actually proves (a real in-flight child must still be observed at least once; it must not merely retry until the timeout silently passes an assertion that never legitimately succeeded). After the fix, run test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs standalone AND at least 3 scripts/test_parallel.sh runs to build confidence, same discipline as rework iteration 1.
acceptance_criteria: AC-5's in-flight-child test replaced with a poll/retry pattern instead of a single fixed sleep+check, with a bounded total wait
The assertion still genuinely proves a real in-flight child is observed, not weakened into an always-pass
At least 3 scripts/test_parallel.sh full-suite runs quoted, not just one

result.notes:
Fix 1 (in scope, AC-5): replaced the fixed `Process.sleep(50)` + single `Task.Supervisor.children/1` check (old lines ~404-407) with a bounded poll/retry loop: `Enum.reduce_while(1..20, [], fn _, _ -> case Task.Supervisor.children(...) do [] -> Process.sleep(10); {:cont, []}; found -> {:halt, found} end end)`. Max total wait is 20 * 10ms = 200ms, well under the call's own `timeout_ms: 300`, so the test still terminates promptly. The final `assert children != []` is unchanged and still requires a genuine non-empty observation was captured during the loop -- it cannot pass without the running script's task actually being seen as an in-flight child at least once.

Fix 2 (found during verification, same file, in owned_modules -- not part of the originally-reported flake but blocking a clean 3-run confirmation of it): while re-running scripts/test_parallel.sh to verify fix 1, discovered a SEPARATE, unrelated, reproduced flake in the same file: 'test behaviour implementation (AC1) execute_with_manifest/2 is exported' (line 30) failed with 'Expected truthy, got false' on `function_exported?(Executor, :execute_with_manifest, 2)` in 2 of the first 4 test_parallel.sh runs (partition 5 both times). Root cause: `function_exported?/3` (`:erlang.function_exported/3`) checks only already-loaded code and does NOT implicitly load the module first, unlike calling a function on it. Under `mix test --partitions`, ExUnit's random async test ordering can make this assertion the very first reference to `Letflow.Engine.Lua.Executor` in that partition's BEAM VM, so the module may not yet be loaded, and the check spuriously returns false. This is a genuine bug in the test's synchronization, not a race in the code under test -- confirmed by `Executor.execute_with_manifest/2` demonstrably existing (grep of lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex:130). Fixed by adding `assert {:module, Executor} = Code.ensure_loaded(Executor)` immediately before the `function_exported?` assertion. This file is explicitly in this handoff's `owned_modules`, and leaving it unfixed would have made a clean 3-run confirmation of fix 1 impossible to obtain honestly, so it was fixed in the same pass rather than deferred silently or hidden.
